stages.rough: Edit the concept. A real small homemade village fountain that works. Keep the low round ring of fieldstones, the dark slate water, the hollow grey log resting on two forked posts, the short hollow spout, and the plank across the rim holding the boot, the ladle and the horseshoe, all turned to pale stone. Keep the first ivory limestone crust on the forks and on a few rim stones, in patches, so the wood and stone stay legible. Remove the woman completely. Make the single stream of water a thick opaque ribbon, not translucent, leaving the open end of the spout and landing on a pale foam ring, with a band of darker wet stone under the spout. What she did passes through objects: a short peeled pole lashed low across two stones in front of a worn flat stone seat on the rim, a homemade toe bar for holding a seated V, its wood rubbed pale. A plain unlit lantern on a stake beside the ring. Water is painted, never drawn: thick opaque ribbons, paler at the core, darker at the edges, no ink line around water, no thin veil, no drizzle, no fine threads, each ribbon from a visible opening to its own pale foam ring, read against dark stone or wood. Warm ivory limestone, never pure white. Everything rounded, no sharp terraces, no steps. Nobody in the image, no people at all, no statue, no body or face shapes in the stone. Footprint unchanged, exactly 2 by 2 tiles, growth goes up and stays inside the canvas. No letters or runes, no hanging cloth, no hard-edged slab, no painted cast shadow, no fog patches, no sheet of grey smoke. Matte, no gloss, no gilding. Feathered natural ground patch, same iso angle, same ink outlines, warm light from the top left.
stages.solid: Paint the same fountain one step further, between the rough and the grand. Now a real mason-built village fountain: a proper round basin of cut stone with a neat coping, on a footing of the old fieldstones. At its centre a stone pillar, wide at the bottom, flat on top, about a head taller than the old forks, with two thick stone spouts and two ribbons of water falling into the basin. The old grey log and one fork remain, built into the pillar, the log's end still running as a third short spout. The limestone has started to eat the mason's work: wide melted-wax flows run down one side of the pillar and over part of the coping. One small scalloped overflow pool has grown on the rim, the first clear turquoise water. The plank with the stone boot, ladle and horseshoe stays, now on the coping. The worn seat becomes a smooth stone seat with an iron toe bar, a chisel left on it. A stiff wooden pennant on a short pole, no fabric. Two plain unlit lanterns on stakes. The new silhouette is the pillar and the real basin. stages.grand: Edit the concept. Prosperity, a fountain the village has invested in and is starting to lose. Keep the central round cut-stone basin, the limestone column, the four scalloped pools around it, the abandoned timber scaffold and the ladder, the bucket. Remove the woman completely; her broom stays, leaning on a pool rim, its bristles turned stiff and pale. Remove the diamond ground edge and the outlined ground. Thin the heavy black contour to the same ink weight as the rough. Reshape the column: lower and much wider, a broad flared skirt of melted-wax flows, an uneven flat crown, no upright pole shape. Limestone now runs over the cut stone, softening the pool rims into scallops, never a set of hard cylinders, and grips the scaffold's legs and the foot of the ladder; a mason's hammer and trowel left on the platform are stuck in the crust, pale stone. The pools hold clear turquoise over a dark slate floor, four pools at most. Add the running water the concept lacks: two thick ribbons from visible openings in the column's crown into the central basin, and one thick overflow from each lip down to the next pool, each on a foam ring, ochre streaks and darker wet stone under each overflow. The old log end still spouts from the column. The plank with the stone boot, ladle and horseshoe stays on a rim. The seat and iron toe bar stay, half crusted. A clan banner stretched on a rigid wooden frame on the platform. Plain unlit lanterns on the scaffold posts. stages.legendary: Paint the same fountain as a marvel, between the grand and the mythic. All of the grand stays: basin, column, four pools, scaffold, ladder, broom, plank with its stone objects. The stone now out-grows its makers: a first great arc of water-polished limestone leaves the column high up and curves down into the basin, thick and rounded, clearly an old jet of water turned to stone, the new silhouette, taller than the column. A real thick ribbon of blue water still runs along its back, and ends on a foam ring. Where it lands, a whole crown of splash stopped in pale stone, a ring of fat rounded lobes. First sign of magic: at the tip of the arc, three big irregular gobs of real water stand still in the air, painted in the same way as the ribbon, against the dark basin behind them. A cold blue shows on the underside of the arc. A clay water jar stands on a ring pad under the arch, at the end of a worn path, for walking with a load on the head. A plain carved shield set into a limestone flow, no symbol on it. stages.mythic: Edit the concept and go much further: the sight the whole village is known for. The basin and footprint stay the same. One single colossal open wave of warm ivory limestone bursts from the round basin, a third taller than the concept, up to the very top of the canvas, tall as a keep, leaning far over to the right so that its crest overhangs the whole basin, an overhang that gives vertigo. It never curls over on itself: an open wave, no spiral, not a shell, not a mushroom, not a horn. Keep the broad back with ochre flow streaks and the thick blue ribbon down the spine. Change the crest: broad and heavy to its end, fringed with fat rounded lobes of stone, remove the long thin strands across the back, nothing like fingers or claws. Thin the heavy black contour to the same ink weight as the rough. Turn the wave a little towards the viewer so its hollow becomes a vast dark wet wall, deep slate going to turquoise, behind everything that falls from the crest. Remove the floating log and all the outlined teardrops. Three thick ribbons of real blue water leave the crest. Two fall all the way, in front of the dark hollow, to foam rings in the basin. The third, thickest, simply stops in mid-air halfway down, and its lower end breaks into about twelve big irregular gobs and blobs of water, standing still at different heights, none the same shape, stretched, wobbling, some still joined by a neck of water, painted exactly like the ribbon with soft pale cores and darker edges and no ink line at all, never a drop icon, never a clean teardrop. Below them, a pale foam ring waits in the basin for water that never arrives. The picture must say this with no motion at all. Strong magic layer, clear by day and by night: the hollow and the basin floor glow from within in cold turquoise, the largest cold area of the village, lighting the underside of the crest and the standing water. Everything earlier survives at the foot, tiny, to give the scale: the old grey log sticking out of the wave's foot, fully encrusted; the four pools turned into scalloped turquoise bowls climbing the left flank, overflowing into each other, and into the frozen splash crown; the great stone arc from the column now a small loop at the base; the scaffold and the ladder swallowed halfway up the flank, far too high to have been reached; the seat and toe bar, the jar on its pad, the broom, the plank with the stone boot, ladle and horseshoe, all pale stone. A plain carved shield with a pale cold light in its surface, no symbol, on the flank. Plain lanterns on old posts.
